lens: F4 Ergonomic — new-contributor cognitive load. Trigger questions: time-to-correct-add-account, typo-failure-mode, error-message-actionability, memorization-burden. Anti-patterns: 8-field-row-with-3-cross-references-and-1-dsl, silent-mismatch-instead-of-error, implicit-conventions-not-declared.

new_contributor_minutes_basis.worst_case_typo_recovery_adds_minutes: +6 to +10 (open .omc/state/settings-drift-report.json, parse JSON-by-eye, locate the offending account_id row, decide whether DriftState::Modified diff field is filled or not). Worst-case journey breaks the ≤15 budget.
new_contributor_minutes_basis.verdict_against_cc1_bar: PASS for happy path (13 ≤ 15). MARGINAL for typo-recovery path because error surfacing is a JSON-file-in-.omc/state rather than a stderr-line at supervisor spawn (see finding F4-3).

typical_new_contributor_journey: Add a new claude account: (1) get an `sref://openbao/<path>` for the account credential, (2) append a single row to `registry/accounts/claude.toml` (schema inherited from v4 §B — not re-declared in v5, so contributor must read v4 §B.2.5 to know the exact field set), (3) run the next supervisor `tick_once` (or wait for cron), which silently invokes `AccountSnapshotProvider::snapshot` → composite `SettingsRenderer::verify` per provider → `render` when `VerifyMode::AutoReconcile`. Expected outcome: `~/.claude/settings.json` is materialized (merged with whatever top-level keys already exist) using the canonical `templates/foundry-supervisor/claude.toml`. The contributor never edits the template — that is workspace-canonical, edit-once-by-architect.

error_message_quality_check.expected_surfacing: stderr line at supervisor startup: `account_id='cluade-prod' rejected: validation error — see field X`
error_message_quality_check.actual_surfacing_per_v5_plan: Unspecified. v5 §B.4 says drifting accounts are EXCLUDED from the snapshot (FailOnDrift) or auto-rendered (AutoReconcile). A typo that breaks parsing surfaces through whatever `parse_template_toml` returns; v5 §B.2.1 declares `SettingsRendererError::InvalidTemplate(String)` whose `String` content is implementation-defined.
error_message_quality_check.verdict: MARGINAL — error type exists, but no plan-level guarantee that the String carries (file_path, line, column, suggestion). Anti-pattern risk: silent-mismatch-instead-of-error if AutoReconcile is the default mode.

error_message_quality_check.expected_surfacing: stderr line: `sref parse failed: scheme expected 'sref', got 'srf' at templates/foundry-supervisor/claude.toml:14 (or registry/accounts/claude.toml:7)`
error_message_quality_check.actual_surfacing_per_v5_plan: `SecretReferenceError` reused from `oya-foundry-account-kernel` (v5 §B.0). Variant detail not duplicated in v5; depends entirely on v4-era variant set. `SecretRefUnresolved(String)` exists. No commitment that the String includes the SOURCE file path.
error_message_quality_check.verdict: MARGINAL — actionability depends on what the upstream `SecretReferenceError::Display` impl emits; v5 doesn't pin a contract.

error_message_quality_check.failure_mode: HookEvent variant declared in `templates/foundry-supervisor/codex.toml` that Codex doesn't recognize (e.g. `SubagentStart` against future Codex schema)
error_message_quality_check.expected_surfacing: compile-time fail in `tests/hook_event_mapping.rs` round-trip test (§A.1.4 pre-mortem (b)); at render-time, `HookEventNotMapped(HookEvent)` is raised.
error_message_quality_check.verdict: PASS — round-trip test is the ergonomic guardrail; contributor sees the issue at CI time, not at runtime.

error_message_quality_check.failure_mode: Drift caused by hand-edit of `~/.claude/settings.json` outside the renderer
error_message_quality_check.expected_surfacing: stderr at next supervisor tick: `account=foo excluded due to drift in ~/.claude/settings.json (key=permissions[0].rule); see .omc/state/settings-drift-report.json or run `cargo run -p oya-dev-cli -- gate validate settings-drift --explain foo`'
error_message_quality_check.actual_surfacing_per_v5_plan: v5 §B.4 commits to writing `.omc/state/settings-drift-report.json` but does NOT commit to emitting a stderr summary at spawn time. v5 §B.5 lane prints exit-1 with non-empty report, but that is CI-time, not workspace-developer-time. Contributor in the loop with a hand-edit has to know that a JSON file in .omc/state/ is where the answer lives.
error_message_quality_check.verdict: FAIL — anti-pattern: silent-mismatch-instead-of-error. Plan should require a one-line stderr surfacing of every account excluded per tick. Recommend acceptance row addition.

error_message_quality_check.expected_surfacing: CI lane `lean-settings-drift` rejects unbumped template with `version=1 but content blake3 changed; bump version to 2`.
error_message_quality_check.actual_surfacing_per_v5_plan: v5 §B.2.1 declares `version: u32` and the SettingsTemplate struct docstring says 'monotonically incremented on schema change' — but the CI lane in §B.5 does NOT specify version-bump enforcement. The 5-step subcommand wiring loads templates, enumerates accounts, verifies, writes report. No `version` bump check.
error_message_quality_check.verdict: MARGINAL — version field exists as a value type contract but the enforcement is absent from the CI lane spec; a new contributor will not know they were supposed to bump it.

error_message_quality_check.failure_mode: Contributor uses an interpolation token in template (e.g. `$HOME` instead of the documented `$WORKSPACE_ROOT`)
error_message_quality_check.expected_surfacing: render-time error: `unknown interpolation token $HOME; supported: $WORKSPACE_ROOT, $HOME_DIR (closest match: did you mean $HOME_DIR?)`
error_message_quality_check.actual_surfacing_per_v5_plan: v5 §B.3 example uses `$WORKSPACE_ROOT` but v5 declares neither the full interpolation grammar nor what happens with unknown tokens. Anti-pattern: implicit-conventions-not-declared.
error_message_quality_check.verdict: FAIL — interpolation grammar is implicit-only. Recommend grammar declaration in B.2.1 or B.3.

that running `tick_once` (or waiting for the supervisor cron) triggers render

memorization_burden.verdict_for_workspace_owner: FAIL against ≤3 bar — but workspace-owner is the expert archetype, so F4 scores against new-contributor archetype. Recommend a `docs/foundry/settings-template/operations.md` (already on the doc-coverage scaffold list per v5 §B.8) explicitly cover these 7 items as a checklist.

anti_pattern_audit.detail: registry/accounts/<provider>.toml row is ≤5 fields with 0 cross-references and 1 mini-DSL (sref://). Inside the ≤8-field, ≤3-xref, ≤1-DSL envelope.

v5 §B.4 commits to writing drift to `.omc/state/settings-drift-report.json` but does NOT commit to stderr-surfacing at supervisor tick time when an account is excluded. A new contributor with a hand-edited ~/.claude/settings.json will see their account silently dropped from the snapshot. This is the canonical F4 anti-pattern. Recommend acceptance row C.31 (additive): every excluded account emits one stderr line at tick start naming the account_id and the drifting key. Also: AutoReconcile mode silently overwrites contributor hand-edits — a one-line stderr per overwrite is the minimal courtesy.

Three implicit conventions: (a) $WORKSPACE_ROOT interpolation grammar is illustrated but never specified (full token set, escape rules, behavior on undefined token). (b) Per-provider merge-vs-replace semantics are described in prose at §B.3 but not codified in the renderer trait contract — a new contributor cannot infer 'will my hand-edit survive?' from reading the type signatures alone. (c) version: u32 bump discipline is documented in a docstring but not enforced anywhere — silent drift hazard. Each should be lifted from prose into either a trait-doc invariant or a CI lane assertion.

findings.summary: Drift-induced account exclusion lacks stderr surfacing (silent-mismatch-instead-of-error).
findings.where: v5 §B.4 paragraph 'An implementation MAY invoke SettingsRenderer::verify ... excluded from the returned Vec<ProviderAccount> ... Drift outcomes are written to .omc/state/settings-drift-report.json'
findings.why_it_matters_for_F4: A new contributor who hand-edits ~/.claude/settings.json (a very plausible first-day action) will see their account silently dropped from RoutePolicy::select with no visible error. They will spend 10-30 minutes debugging 'why is my account ignored?' before they think to look in .omc/state/. This is the worst-case F4 anti-pattern.
findings.recommendation: Add a non-MAY clause: `AccountSnapshotProvider::snapshot() impls that exclude accounts due to drift MUST emit one stderr line per excluded account in the form `[supervisor] account=<id> excluded due to drift; key=<first_mismatched_key>; details=.omc/state/settings-drift-report.json`. Add an acceptance row (e.g. C.31) asserting this.
evidence_required: new acceptance row testing stderr line shape

findings.summary: registry/accounts/<provider>.toml field schema is not re-declared in v5 — new contributor must spelunk v4 to know what to type.
findings.where: v5 §B.4 and §B.5 reference `registry/accounts/<provider>.toml` repeatedly but never re-show its row schema; v4 §B.2.5 owns it.
findings.why_it_matters_for_F4: The plan correctly identifies adding-an-account as the dominant new-contributor journey, then leaves the most-important schema undocumented in the same file. Forces a 4-minute v4-spelunk into the 13-minute happy path budget.
findings.recommendation: Add a 6-line snippet to v5 §B.3 (or a new §B.3a) showing the canonical 1-row example of `registry/accounts/claude.toml` with the field set inherited from v4. Even a one-line citation `# schema: see v4 §B.2.5 ProviderAccount` is better than the current silence.
evidence_required: v5 plan diff adding the snippet

findings.summary: Template interpolation grammar ($WORKSPACE_ROOT) is illustrative-only, not specified (implicit-conventions-not-declared).
findings.where: v5 §B.3 example uses `$WORKSPACE_ROOT/tools/foundry-supervisor-stop-hook`; no grammar declaration anywhere in v5.
findings.why_it_matters_for_F4: Workspace-owner archetype (secondary F4 audience) cannot tell whether `$HOME`, `${WORKSPACE_ROOT}`, `~`, `%WORKSPACE_ROOT%` are supported; cannot tell what happens with an unknown token (silent literal? render-time error? CI-time error?). Failure mode is invisible.
findings.recommendation: Add to §B.2.1 a `InterpolationGrammar` value type or to §B.3 a 4-line BNF: tokens supported are `${WORKSPACE_ROOT}` and `${HOME_DIR}` (or whatever the chosen set is); unknown token → `SettingsRendererError::InvalidTemplate("unknown token '${X}' at <file>:<line>; supported: ...")`.

findings.summary: AutoReconcile mode silently overwrites workspace-owner hand-edits without a courtesy stderr line.
findings.where: v5 §B.4 `VerifyMode::AutoReconcile` semantics: 'the implementation calls SettingsRenderer::render for the drifting account, then includes it in the snapshot'.
findings.why_it_matters_for_F4: Workspace-owner archetype runs supervisor in AutoReconcile during onboarding to avoid having to manually re-render after every account add. If they hand-edit ~/.claude/settings.json (e.g. for a 1-off test) and supervisor ticks, the hand-edit is silently overwritten. They lose work invisibly.
findings.recommendation: AutoReconcile MUST emit a stderr line per overwrite: `[supervisor] account=<id> auto-reconciled; <N> file(s) overwritten; previous content backed up to .omc/state/settings-overwrite-backup/<account_id>/<timestamp>/`. Adds a backup-on-overwrite obligation. Cheap to implement, eliminates the destructive-default footgun.

findings.summary: Template `version: u32` bump discipline is not CI-enforced (implicit-conventions-not-declared).
findings.where: v5 §B.2.1 docstring 'monotonically incremented on schema change'; v5 §B.5 CI lane subcommand wiring (5 steps) has no version-bump assertion.
findings.why_it_matters_for_F4: A workspace-owner who edits `claude.toml` and forgets the `version` bump will pass CI and silently produce a fleet-wide settings drift that hashes-differ but version-matches. Drift detection becomes spurious — 'why does every account fail verify after my PR?'
findings.recommendation: CI lane `lean-settings-drift` to compare `version` field against `git log -- templates/foundry-supervisor/<provider>.toml`; if content changed without a version bump, fail with `template content_blake3 changed but version did not; bump version from N to N+1`.

findings.summary: HookEvent → provider event name mapping is not discoverable via CLI (forces source-reading).
findings.where: v5 §A.1.4 pre-mortem (b) introduces per-provider `HookEventMap`; mapping table is tested in `tests/hook_event_mapping.rs` but never surfaced as an `oya-dev-cli` subcommand.
findings.why_it_matters_for_F4: Workspace-owner archetype asking 'what does Stop map to on Codex?' must read renderer source or run a test. Discoverability cost: ~5 minutes per question. Not a blocker but a steady tax.
findings.recommendation: Add `oya-dev-cli settings-template explain-hooks --provider codex` (or similar) that prints the HookEventMap table. Adds 1 line to v5.18 grit-unit scope. Cheap.

findings.summary: Plan correctly partitions new-contributor cognitive load between account-add (1 file, 3 memorizations) and template-edit (1 file, 7 memorizations) — workspace-canonical pattern is the right F4 stance.
findings.where: v5 §B.0 implicit (templates/ is workspace-canonical; registry/accounts/ is per-account) + §B.3 first paragraph.
findings.why_it_matters_for_F4: The plan correctly identifies that the daily new-contributor task is account-add, not template-edit. Cognitive load is concentrated on the rarer template-edit (expert) path. This is the right F4 trade-off — keep the common case cheap.
findings.recommendation: No change. Note this strength in synthesis.

ergonomic_strengths: Single-file edit for add-account is the right baseline (1 cross-reference, ≤5 fields).
Workspace-canonical templates eliminate per-account drift by construction — there is no per-account override-of-templates surface to learn.
RISK rows (§B.6 R1/R2/R3) honestly downgrade Gemini hook support to no-op rather than inventing aspirational capability — new-contributor surprise is minimized.
Pre-mortem (b) catches the HookEvent vocabulary mismatch at CI time via fixture round-trip, not at runtime.
Atomic tempfile+rename for renders means partial-write failure-modes don't corrupt the on-disk file — contributor never sees a half-written settings.json.
Idempotent re-render (C.28) means accidentally running `tick_once` twice is harmless, removing a class of fear-of-action paralysis for new contributors.
ergonomic_risks_summary: Drift exclusion silent at tick stderr — finding F4-1 (medium).
registry/accounts/<provider>.toml schema not re-declared in v5 — finding F4-2 (medium).
AutoReconcile destructive default without backup-on-overwrite — finding F4-4 (low).
Template version bump discipline not CI-enforced — finding F4-5 (low).
HookEventMap not introspectable via CLI — finding F4-6 (low).

verdict.rationale: The dominant new-contributor journey (add-account) lands at 13 minutes / 1-file-edit / 3 memorizations — inside the CC-1 ≤15-minute, ≤3-memorization F4 bar. All 6 findings are quality-of-life improvements that should be incorporated but none block kernel public API approval. The medium-severity findings (F4-1 stderr surfacing, F4-2 schema re-citation) are cheap to address and would materially reduce typo-recovery time.
